title: Deja Vu: Contextual Sparsity for Efficient LLMs at Inference Time
technique: input-dependent contextual sparsity (attention heads and MLP neurons) predicted per layer by lightweight predictors, with asynchronous lookahead prediction and fused hardware-aware sparse kernels

optimized_metrics.evidence: The goal is to reduce the generation latency of LLMs by exploiting contextual sparsity.
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: Average per-token latency (ms) with batch size 1 on 8 A100-80GB (Fig. 7 caption)

optimized_metrics.evidence: speed up LLM inference in wall-clock time without compromising LLM's quality or in-context learning ability

headline_claim.text: DEJA VU can reduce the inference latency of OPT-175B by over 2x compared to the state-of-the-art FasterTransformer, and over 6x compared to the widely used Hugging Face implementation, without compromising model quality.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 7 average per-token latency (ms), batch size 1, 8xA100-80G; Table 3 latency breakdown
Fig 6, Tables 4-7 zero-shot accuracy and perplexity vs sparsity
Fig 8, 11: union contextual sparsity vs batch size

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Average per-token latency (ms) with batch size 1 on 8 A100-80GB with NVLink when generating sequences with prompt lengths 128, 256, 512, and 1024, using FP16.
metric_definitions.notes: per-token decode latency for a single sequence; prompt-phase excluded from focus ("Latency breakdown of generating 1 token" Table 3, setting batch size 1, prompt length 128)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Union contextual sparsity (fraction of neurons/heads that are not used by any of the inputs in the batch)
metric_definitions.notes: shows benefit shrinks as batch grows

load_regime: batch=1 for headline ("this paper focuses on latency-sensitive settings"); larger batches only analysed via union sparsity
tradeoff_acknowledged: Accuracy vs sparsity: no accuracy drop until ~75% sparsity; sparsity benefit shrinks at larger batch (union of active neurons grows); prefill-phase not accelerated in the same way.
extractor_notes: Latency here is single-stream per-token decode latency. Note: the Deja Vu text itself says it targets latency-sensitive small-batch settings.
load_class_quote: Figure 7. Average per-token latency (ms) with batch size 1 on 8 A100-80GB; "this paper focuses on latency-sensitive settings" (§5.2)
